title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Pre-upgrade sync to finalize canary plan and confirm network mitigations. Reviewed NAT EIP pinning vs VPC peering, maintenance window logistics, canary metrics (p95/p99/KV hit rate), KMS audit requirements, and next steps for quantization evaluation and runbook delivery.
action_items: Rita Gomez - upload final 72h VPC flow logs and NAT rotation dump by 2026-12-18 12:00 UTC
Alex Chen - circulate final upgrade runbook, restart list, and CIDR whitelist by 2026-12-18 10:00 UTC
Priya Rao - deliver canary harness and prompt-level eval sheet with baseline quality metrics by 2026-12-19
Samir Patel - confirm SOC2 scoping questions and required artifacts by 2026-12-18
Evan Cho - confirm ops contacts for the maintenance window and standby plan by 2026-12-18
next_steps: Run pre-upgrade canary (dev subnet) to capture p95/p99 and KV hit rate
Customer to decide EIP pinning or peering and communicate preference
Redwood to run quantization eval and share delta report
Redwood to provide final whitelist CIDRs and maintenance checklist
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Morning team, quick 30-minute sync to lock the canary plan and ensure everybody's comfortable with the upgrade window.
[00:07] James Miller: morning alex. ops can make the tentatively scheduled 12-18 03:00-05:00 UTC window if we get the runbook and 24h notice.
[00:16] Alex Chen: understood. we'll send the final runbook this morning. rollback criteria: we roll back if p99 increases more than 20% or error rate >0.5% over baseline during canary.
[00:30] Priya Rao: on canary specifics: start at 2% traffic with a synthetic replay for 20 minutes, gather p95/p99, requests/sec, KV cache hit rate, and qualitative prompt outputs; if stable ramp to 10% then 50%.
[00:44] Rita Gomez: we've reproduced the NAT rotation in staging; our TGW auto-assigns eips causing ephemeral source IP changes. we can either pin EIPs on the NAT or open VPC peering, security prefers peering but needs a diagram.
[00:58] Samir Patel: right, peering preferred from security, but we need architecture diagram and least-privilege IAM policies. also KMS must remain customer-controlled.
[01:10] Alex Chen: confirmed - Redwood supports customer-managed KMS; we'll provide integration guide and a flow diagram. Marta will attach SOC2 excerpts masked to your deployment.
[01:21] Lena Wu: about KV cache miss rate - what are we expecting if routing is stable?
[01:25] Priya Rao: with stable source IPs we saw cache hit improve from ~78% to ~90% in tests, which yielded ~10-15% improvement in p95.
[01:36] James Miller: good. regarding quantization, we want a side-by-side run post-upgrade. can we schedule that as a second canary?
[01:42] Priya Rao: yes, we'll script non-quantized and quantized runs and provide a diff sheet with quality metrics and flag any regressions.
[01:51] Evan Cho: ops question: how long does each node restart take and will cache persist across restarts?
[01:56] Priya Rao: node restart is typically 3-5 minutes, persisted cache blobs remain; warm-up takes about 10-15 minutes of representative traffic. we'll document per-node expected downtime in the runbook.
[02:08] Rita Gomez: i'll upload the flow logs and NAT events to the shared bucket and grant access to the Redwood SEs.
[02:14] Alex Chen: thanks Rita. once we have those logs we'll correlate with our traces and isolate whether the 5xxs are network or service.
[02:22] Samir Patel: audit logs - we need 12-month retention with tamper-evidence and KMS usage reporting. can you confirm object-lock support?
[02:31] Alex Chen: yes, S3 object-lock supported and audit exports can include KMS usage logs. we'll include configuration options in the runbook.
[02:39] Marta Lopez: observability note: the private console replicates token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards; telemetry can be forwarded to your Datadog/Splunk and redaction rules applied.
[02:52] Lena Wu: will traces include PII by default?
[02:55] Priya Rao: no, traces can be configured to redact payloads and enable field-level filtering; we'll provide standard redaction templates.
[03:04] James Miller: final question: after the post-upgrade canary if metrics look stable, what's the rollback cadence?
[03:09] Priya Rao: we'll keep automatic fallback and allow manual rollback if you request; nodes will be able to switch to runtime 2.0 image quickly. we'll run a final validation sweep after any rollback.
[03:20] Alex Chen: recap: Rita uploads logs; Alex sends runbook and CIDRs; Priya delivers canary harness and eval sheet; Samir sends SOC2 points; Evan confirms ops standby list. we'll reconvene after canary results.
[03:33] James Miller: sounds good, we'll decide on EIP vs peering and notify you.
[03:37] Priya Rao: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[03:40] Alex Chen: thanks all, talk soon.
[03:41] -- end of recording --

Note: Transcript is a Fireflies-style transcript with occasional misattributions and imperfect punctuation.
